svg.title: Burst fusion training flow
svg.text: Training: one network for every dose, from raw drifting frames only
No clean image, no averaged target, no pre-registered data. One burst per sample; everything below happens inside that burst.
subset S of m frames, m ∈ {1..15}
loss ‖ W_h f(x_S, m) − y_h ‖² + 4 · ‖ S W_h f(x_S, m) − S y_h ‖² (interior, 2-px border dropped)
y_h is not in S, so its noise is independent of the input: the optimum is E[y_h | m frames] -- Noise2Noise, extended to a burst.
Why warp the prediction and not the frame:
the prediction is smooth, so resampling it
costs nothing; resampling the noisy target
would average its noise and bias the loss.
Why t = m: the estimator that is right for
one frame over-smooths a 16-frame mean and
vice versa -- the dose is part of the input.
Ablations, one config line each: align: none (average the drifting frames as they are), align: truth (the generator's recorded drift), condition_on_level: false (t = 1 at every dose).
